title: SLO 90-day mini-pilot and ops handoff notes
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is an internal working note for running a focused 90-day SLO mini-pilot across two product surfaces (hosted inference API and a Dedicated model pool). Goal: validate operational practices (alerting, canary rollback, observability dashboards, oncall runbooks) and produce a lightweight handoff checklist for feature teams to adopt SLOs without large program overhead.

Why a 90-day mini-pilot?
- Rapid learning cycle: shorter than a full org-wide rollout and fits within product quarterly milestones.
- Focused scope: reduces noise; we can iterate on telemetry and runbooks with two teams before scaling.
- Outcome-driven: deliver a reproducible handoff artifact and three small automation improvements.

Success criteria (must be measurable):
- Baseline and target SLO defined and agreed (error-rate or p99 latency) for both surfaces by Day 7.
- Dashboards ingesting necessary signals end-to-end (ingest, transform, retention) within Day 21.
- Canary rollout and automated rollback tested end-to-end (failure injection) by Day 45.
- Oncall runbooks exercised in at least two simulated incidents and two real incidents with post-incident notes and retro by Day 90.
- Handoff package (runbook + dashboards + ticket templates + one pager) accepted by platform and product leads on Day 90.

Pilot timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (prep): align stakeholders, pick service owners, confirm telemetry ownership, create JIRA epic.
- Week 1: define SLOs and SLI formulas, baseline measurement window.
- Weeks 2–3: telemetry gaps work (metrics, traces, logs); dashboard drafts.
- Week 4: oncall playbook draft + basic automation (alert dedupe, suppression).
- Weeks 5–6: run a controlled canary rollout (limited percent traffic) and validate metrics/alerts.
- Week 7–10: deliberate failure injections (latency spike, mem pressure) and test rollback playbook.
- Week 11–12: collect incident drills, write retros, finalize handoff artifacts.

Detailed roles and responsibilities (lightweight):
- Pilot Lead: Priya Desai — program ops, stakeholder cadence, decisions on scope.
- Telemetry Lead: Marcus Li — metrics ingestion, dashboard ownership, retention checks.
- Platform Integration: Ethan Park — canary automation, routing policies, rollout hooks.
- Feature Owner Liaison: Nina Kaur — product team coordination, release windows, acceptance.
- SRE Oncall SME: Olivia Grant — runbook authoring, incident drill facilitation.

Key deliverables (atomic items we can hand off):
- SLO spec (one-pager per service): intent, SLI definition, measurement window, error budget policy.
- Minimal dashboard set: SLI trend, error budget burn rate, top contributing errors, p95/p99 latency histograms.
- Canary playbook: pre-checks, traffic shifting steps, rollback triggers and automate-able steps.
- Runbook template w/ escalation matrix and Slack/PagerDuty snippets.
- Postmortem template mapped back to SLO impact columns (does this incident affect SLO? cadence, mitigation).

Telemetry checklist (common gaps to look for):
- Does the service emit explicit success/failure counters? If not, add a lightweight counter.
- Are latency quantiles emitted by the application or inference runtime (preferred) or only at proxy layer? Track both if feasible.
- Does the platform pipeline preserve labels (model_version, deployment_zone, route)? Missing labels = high debugging cost.
- Retention: raw traces for 7 days, metrics at 10s granularity for 14 days (adjustable).

Alerting & policies (draft):
- Alert types: SLI threshold (burn), SLI drop (step change), infrastructure saturation (node CPU/GPU), deployment errors (bad rollout).
- Burn alerts: fire at 25%/50%/90% of error budget in a rolling window. Define actions per threshold.
- Suppression windows: automated suppressions for planned maintenance (link to release tickets).
- PagerDuty routing: primary SRE oncall -> feature-owner rotation -> platform eng escalation.

Canary and rollback triggers (concrete):
- Canary window length: 10 minutes minimum for traffic-based checks; require 3 consecutive metric samples (10s cadence) within thresholds.
- Failure triggers: 2x baseline error-rate OR p99 latency > SLO target * 1.5 for the canary window.
- Automated rollback: use platform automation to shift traffic back to previous revision; avoid automatic rollback during critical customer windows (opt-in).

Experiment list (for the 90-day window):
1) Prefix cache warmup: measure impact of pre-warming KV cache on p99; success = 15% p99 reduction for 95th percentile customers.
2) Quantized fallback routing: route low-tier traffic to a quantized variant under high load, observe error budget impact.
3) Alert dedupe rule: test dedupe to reduce noisy pages by 40% without missing true incidents.

Communications and meeting cadence (practical):
- Weekly pilot sync (30m): progress, blockers, decisions. Owner: Pilot Lead.
- Bi-weekly stakeholder demo (45m): show dashboards, canary playback, failing tests.
- Incident drills: schedule two timeboxed drills with SRE and feature owners, capture retro notes.
- Final handoff review: 60m sign-off meeting with product, platform, and SRE leads.

Risks and mitigations (honest notes):
- Risk: telemetry instrumentation takes longer than expected. Mitigation: identify a minimal SLI fallback (proxy-level success metric) so we can run early experiments.
- Risk: feature teams treat SLOs as another checkbox. Mitigation: tie a small product KPI (release gating or SLA callout) to the pilot acceptance.
- Risk: noisy alerts drown out signal. Mitigation: enforce alerting templates and one-week suppression during major releases.

Open questions (to resolve in Week 0–1):
- Which specific endpoints/routes constitute customer-visible success for the hosted API? (Product to list top 5)
- Agree on SLO window (30d vs 90d) and whether to publish to external customers.
- Does Dedicated pool require separate SLO definitions for hardware-induced tail latency?

Quick notes to self (Priya):
- Keep artifacts small: one-pager SLOs, not a 20-page playbook.
- Capture every drill with timestamps and replay steps (high value for debugging).
- Start with synthetic failure injected via canary traffic rather than real-customer impact.

Handoff checklist (what we hand to feature teams at the end):
- SLO one-pager (signed by product lead)
- Dashboard links + brief walkthrough video (5–8 min recording)
- Runbook + PagerDuty snippets
- Canary playbook + automation runbook
- Incident templates & retro template mapped to SLO impact
- Short backlog of recommended follow-ups (telemetry quality, alerts tuning, automation tasks)

Appendix: quick artifact examples (copy/paste templates)
- SLO line: "Availability SLO: successful/responsive inference calls >= 99.9% measured over 30d window; SLI = (success_count) / (total_count) where success_count excludes client-side timeouts and cancelled requests."
- Basic rollback snippet: "platform rollout --target previous_revision --grace 30s && notify #reliability-ops with link to rollback-runbook"

Next actions (immediate):
- Create JIRA epic and link pilot participants (Priya, Marcus, Ethan, Nina, Olivia) — due Fri 2026-06-05.
- Product owners to send list of top endpoints for SLO candidate evaluation — due Mon 2026-06-08.
- Telemetry lead to publish current baseline metrics for both surfaces — due Tue 2026-06-09.

End of note. This doc will be iterated; please add comments inline or push updates to the linked Confluence page.
